name: Schedule sand hauling to pads
summary: Every tonne of frac sand reaches the pad by truck from an in-basin terminal, about 3,000 loads a month in an ordinary month. Logistics coordinators turn each day's stage schedule into hourly load slots, send haul orders to contract carriers and track trucks and storage levels; sand operators on the pad check each load ticket and watch the trailer blow its sand into wellsite storage; the coordinator then matches tickets to orders before carriers are paid. A full pad leaves trucks on paid stand-by and an empty one stops a fleet worth thousands of dollars an hour, so road bans, storms, screen-outs and carrier shortages all turn into re-planning by phone.

baseline.org_archetype: A TSX-listed Canadian pressure pumper with about 1,350 employees, six to eight 24-hour frac crews, a 70-person supply chain department in Calgary and at district bases, an ERP with procurement and inventory, and spreadsheets, email and phone for day-to-day logistics.
baseline.notes: Trucks belong to third-party carriers; the company's people are the coordinators and the sand operators on each frac crew.

unit_of_work: one truckload of frac sand (about 38 tonnes on a B-train pneumatic trailer)
trigger: A pad's stage schedule for the next day sets the sand needed by mesh and hour.
end_state: The load is in wellsite storage, its ticket is matched and approved for payment; or the load is sent elsewhere.

volume.seasonality: Peak from January to mid-March, near zero during spring break-up road bans, rising again from June.

evidence.note: About 112,000 tonnes a month (organisation file) at about 38 tonnes a load. Payload is the author's estimate for a B-train pneumatic in Alberta; US pneumatic trucks carry about 46,000 lb (aogr_last_mile) so loads would be higher with smaller trucks. Comparable volumes in step_2021.

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Same winter peak as the organisation file process entry; multiplier is the author's estimate.
Around-the-clock desk: one to two coordinators on shift for hauling across six to eight fleets, plus ticket reconciliation; author's estimate from 14 coordinators in the organisation file.
Sand operators on each 24-hour frac crew spend part of each shift receiving trucks; the rest of their time is in the on-site proppant and job execution processes. Author's estimate.

systems.name: Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)

resources.name: Wellsite proppant storage and conveyor units

steps.name: Receive daily stage and sand schedule
steps.description: The logistics coordinator receives the next day's stage schedule for the pad from the frac operations coordinator and the field supervisor: stages planned, tonnes per stage by mesh and expected pump hours. Minutes are this load's share of handling the whole schedule.

error.defect_description: Stage count or tonnes copied wrongly.

evidence.note: Stages of about 54-83 tonnes each (step_2021) set the loads per day; per-load share of the work is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Build hourly haul schedule
steps.description: The coordinator turns the stage plan into hourly load slots by mesh and terminal on the dispatch board, so that wellsite storage never runs dry and never overflows. They allow for the round trip from the terminal and the unloading time at the pad.

error.defect_description: Wrong mesh sequence or too many loads booked in one hour.

evidence.note: One pad can need more than 130 truckloads a day (aogr_last_mile); per-load minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check road bans and route
steps.description: The coordinator checks the provincial and municipal road ban lists, lease road conditions reported by the customer and any weight restrictions on the route from the terminal to the pad.

error.defect_description: A newly posted municipal ban is missed.

next.condition: road ban or lease road restriction

evidence.note: Bans set by the province on highways and by municipalities on local roads, with a notification service (ab_road_bans).

steps.name: Adjust loads for a road ban
steps.description: The coordinator lowers the payload to the banned percentage, which adds trucks, or reroutes through roads without bans, or asks the carrier to apply to the Central Permit Office for a road ban exemption permit. They update the haul schedule with the extra loads.

error.defect_description: Truck dispatched over the allowed weight.

control.basis: Alberta Commercial Vehicle Dimension and Weight Regulation and municipal road ban orders

evidence.note: Road ban exemption permits through the Central Permit Office (ab_road_bans); share and waits are estimates.

steps.name: Send haul order to carrier
steps.description: The coordinator sends the carrier's dispatcher the load slot, terminal, mesh, tonnes, pad location, lease directions and site contact by email, text or a shared dispatch sheet.

error.defect_description: Wrong pad or LSD location sent.

evidence.note: Dispatch of a carrier network of more than 300 third-party trucks by a 24/7 desk (source_logistics).

steps.name: Carrier accepts and assigns a truck
steps.description: The carrier's dispatcher confirms the load and assigns a driver and pneumatic trailer, or says no truck is free for that slot.

evidence.note: Share of refused loads is the author's estimate; truck shortages are worst in the winter peak.

steps.name: Find an alternative carrier
steps.description: The coordinator phones other approved carriers on the list to cover the slot, checks that the new carrier is set up for the customer's site, and moves the order.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Truck goes to the terminal and loads
steps.description: At the slot time the driver goes to the terminal, queues for the loading spout, is loaded and weighed, and receives a load ticket showing terminal, mesh, lot and net tonnes.

error.defect_description: Wrong mesh loaded at the terminal.

evidence.note: Terminals monitor loading wait times (source_logistics). Wait covers the time until the booked slot plus the terminal queue; author's estimate.

steps.name: Haul to the pad
steps.description: The truck drives from the terminal to the pad on highways and lease roads, typically one to four hours each way in northern Alberta and northeast BC.

evidence.note: Longer terminal-to-wellsite trips noted in 2022 (source_q4_2022); hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Track truck and storage levels
steps.description: While trucks are on the road the coordinator watches carrier ETAs by phone and app and the sand operator's storage levels, and moves slots earlier or later when pumping speeds up or stops.

next.condition: storm, fog or icy lease road

evidence.note: Phone and app tracking between dispatch, carriers and terminals (aogr_last_mile, source_logistics); branch shares are estimates.

steps.name: Truck held by weather
steps.description: The truck pulls over or waits at the lease entrance until a storm, fog or icy lease road clears and the customer reopens the road.

evidence.note: Weather delays in December 2021 and extreme cold in January 2022 (step_2021); durations are estimates.

steps.name: Decide whether to hold or divert a truck
steps.description: When the pad cannot take sand because storage is full or pumping has stopped for a screen-out, wireline delay or breakdown, the coordinator decides with the field supervisor whether the truck waits on stand-by or goes to another pad or back to the terminal. Stand-by hours become demurrage on the carrier's invoice.

error.defect_description: Stand-by not recorded, so the demurrage claim cannot be checked.

next.condition: truck diverted under a new haul order

evidence.note: Carriers bill stand-by or demurrage when trucks wait to unload (aogr_last_mile); shares are estimates.

steps.name: Check in truck at the pad
steps.description: The sand operator meets the driver at the sand area, confirms the driver has the customer's site orientation and required tickets and PPE, and guides the truck into an unloading position away from the pumping area.

control.basis: Customer site safety orientation and hazard assessment (Alberta OHS Code Part 2) before entering an active frac location

evidence.note: Pneumatic operations typically keep about a dozen trucks queued at the pad (aogr_last_mile); wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check load ticket against the order
steps.description: The sand operator reads the load ticket and compares mesh, supplier lot and tonnes with the haul order and the bin that has room. A wrong mesh or missing ticket is stopped here.

error.defect_description: Ticket accepted for the wrong mesh.

evidence.note: Ticket checking by sand operators is described in the organisation file on-site proppant process; share is an estimate.

steps.name: Resolve a wrong or undocumented load
steps.description: The coordinator and sand operator decide whether the load can go into another bin, must go to another pad that uses that mesh, or goes back to the terminal, and they inform the carrier and the terminal.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Unload sand into wellsite storage
steps.description: The driver connects the trailer and blows the sand into the storage unit for that mesh while the sand operator watches bin levels, dust and hose connections and stops the transfer when the bin is full.

error.defect_description: Sand blown into the wrong bin and mixed.

control.basis: Respirable silica dust and pressurised hose controls under the company's code of practice (Alberta OHS Code)

evidence.note: Pneumatic unloading takes 40-70 minutes, about 45 on average (aogr_last_mile); the operator's attention is part of that time (author's estimate).

steps.name: Sign ticket and record tonnes on location
steps.description: The sand operator signs the driver's load ticket, keeps a copy, and adds the tonnes by mesh to the on-site sand inventory sheet used to compare sand on location with stages left.

error.defect_description: Tonnes added to the wrong mesh column.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Update the sand tracker
steps.description: The coordinator updates the pad's sand tracker with the delivered load and storage levels, and adds or cancels later slots to match the stages left.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Carrier submits daily ticket batch
steps.description: At the end of the day or shift the carrier sends scans or photos of signed load tickets and any stand-by hours claimed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile tickets with haul orders
steps.description: The coordinator matches each ticket to its haul order and the sand operator's receipt: tonnes, terminal, pad, and stand-by hours against the hold decision. Matched tickets are marked for payment.

control.basis: Load tickets matched to haul orders and site receipts before carrier invoices are paid

next.condition: missing ticket, weight difference or disputed stand-by

evidence.note: Demurrage charges and ticket matching are a known part of last-mile cost (aogr_last_mile); shares are estimates.

steps.name: Query carrier on a ticket difference
steps.description: The coordinator emails or phones the carrier about the missing ticket, weight difference or stand-by claim, and agrees a correction or a reduced charge.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve tickets for accounts payable
steps.description: The coordinator approves the matched tickets and stand-by charges in the ERP against the carrier's blanket order, charges the haul to the customer's job, and passes the batch to accounts payable.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Road ban restriction
exceptions.description: Spring or wet-weather bans cut payloads or close lease roads; more trucks or a permit are needed.

exceptions.name: No truck available
exceptions.description: The carrier cannot cover the slot and the coordinator finds another carrier.

exceptions.name: Pad cannot receive
exceptions.description: Storage full or pumping stopped; the truck waits on paid stand-by or is diverted.

exceptions.name: Weather hold
exceptions.description: Storm, fog or icy lease road holds the truck before the pad.

exceptions.name: Ticket dispute
exceptions.description: Missing ticket, weight difference or stand-by claim queried with the carrier before payment.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from haul order to ticket approved for payment
benchmarks.population: Sand truckloads to WCSB frac pads, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: haul orders are booked up to a day ahead of the slot, the load reaches the pad within a shift of its slot, and tickets come in daily batches that are reconciled and approved over the next one to two days.
Trade press figure.

pain_points.description: Pneumatic unloading of 40-70 minutes per truck means trucks queue at busy pads and run up stand-by charges.
Schedules are rebuilt by phone and spreadsheet every time pumping speeds up or stops, so coordinators spend their shifts moving slots.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of 2019-2022 practice before app-based dispatch was widespread.

pain_points.description: Matching thousands of paper or photographed load tickets to orders and stand-by claims is slow and error-prone.

evidence.note: Organisation file notes heavy ticket matching in accounts payable; author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Customer job and permitting delays and longer haul distances cut truck productivity.

sources.title: 'Last Mile' Solutions Enhance Efficiency, Reliability Of Proppant Supply Chain (K. Fisher)
sources.supports: Pneumatic truck about 46,000 lb; pneumatic unloading 40-70 minutes, about 45 minutes on average; about a dozen trucks typically queued at the pad; one pad can need more than 130 truckloads a day; carriers bill stand-by or demurrage when trucks wait; shipment tracking through phone apps instead of calls between dispatchers, carriers and terminals; last mile up to a third of delivered sand cost; rail cars of 200,000-220,000 lb and unit trains of 110-120 cars. US conditions in 2017.

sources.title: Last-Mile Logistics
sources.supports: 24/7 dispatch team using real-time technology to monitor inventory and wait times at loading and unloading; own trucks plus a network of more than 300 third-party trucks; more than 2.0 million tonnes of proppant and other materials delivered a year; side-binder hopper and other trailer types; carriers with provincial, prorate, IFTA or oilfield exemption permit licensing.

sources.title: Source Energy Services Reports Q4 2022 and Year End Results
sources.supports: 2,845,600 tonnes of sand sold in 2022, up 15% on 2021; last-mile trucking volumes fell in Q4 2022 because of customer job and permitting delays while longer terminal-to-wellsite trips raised revenue; higher repairs on the railcar fleet; supply contracts renewed with pricing reflecting the 2022 environment; risks of rail line interruptions and reduced railcar availability.

sources.title: Road bans
sources.supports: Road bans reduce maximum allowed weights on roads during weak or thawing conditions; provincial bans on highways and municipal bans on local roads; spring heavy-haul period triggered by thaw depth of at least 25 cm, post-thaw from about June 16; one-window notification service for ban orders; Road Ban Exemption Permit Request to the Central Permit Office.

sources.title: STEP Energy Services Ltd. Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End 2021 Results
sources.supports: Canadian fracturing: 1,012,000 tonnes of proppant in 2021 (776,000 in 2020), 977 operating days, proppant per stage 54 tonnes (Q4 2021) to 83 tonnes (2021); product and hauling costs rose with company-supplied proppant; costs rose late in 2021 with supply chain disruptions; weather delays in late December 2021 and extreme cold in January 2022; spring break-up restricts equipment moves; US segment cites inflation on chemicals, proppant and spare parts.

assumptions: Unit of work is one truckload; planning and scheduling minutes are this load's share of work done for a whole pad-day.
All trucks belong to contract carriers; carrier steps carry no company touch time, and their drive and queue time is shown as waits.
Payload of about 38 tonnes per B-train pneumatic load is the author's estimate; no Canadian payload figure was opened.
Branch shares (road bans 10%, weather 6%, pad not ready 6%) are averages across the year; they are higher in winter and at break-up.
Wellsite storage is tied up only during unloading here; holding sand for pumping belongs to the on-site proppant process.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file (wage x 1.35).
